name: timestep-sepsis
title: BioGears time step: accuracy and speed in a severe infection
question: Over the first 6 h of the severe infection (McDaniel et al. 2019's sepsis model, a slow process run at 60 s updates), how far do 0.04 and 0.08 s solver steps drift from BioGears' validated 0.02 s, and how much faster are they?
hypothesis: The inflammatory response barely depends on the step (pathogen within 0.2 %, tissue integrity within 0.001), and hemodynamics stay within about 2 mmHg and 20 mL of the 0.02 s run, but lactate does not: it climbs to about 10 mM at 0.04 s and 26 mM at 0.08 s while the 0.02 s run stays near 1.5 mM, so a sepsis run with a step above 0.02 s reports hyperlactatemia that isn't there. The larger steps run about 1.9 and 2.8 times faster.
objective: Run biogears_sepsis (severe, StandardMale@0s, InfectionModerate water and meal schedule, 6 h at 60 s updates) at time_step_s 0.02, 0.04 and 0.08, and compare each with the 0.02 s run.

readouts.name: irreversible-state
readouts.description: BioGears reported an irreversible state; the engine is no longer advanced.

readouts.name: time-step
readouts.description: BioGears' solver step of the run (recorded so figures can tell runs apart)

units_and_time.scale: one recorded row per 60 s update (n_steps 360 = 6 h)

units_and_time.note: BioGears' solver step (time_step_s); BioGears is validated at 0.02 s and fails at 0.1 s or more.

expected_behavior.name: inflammation-is-step-independent
expected_behavior.condition: every sample within 0.2 % (pathogen) and 0.001 (tissue integrity) of the 0.02 s run

expected_behavior.name: hemodynamics-stay-close
expected_behavior.condition: every sample within 3 mmHg (MAP, SBP) and 25 mL (blood volume) of the 0.02 s run, the error larger at 0.08 than at 0.04 s

expected_behavior.name: lactate-breaks-above-0-02
expected_behavior.condition: the 0.02 s run stays below 2 mM; 0.04 s ends above 5 mM and 0.08 s higher still

expected_behavior.name: larger-steps-run-faster
expected_behavior.condition: the 0.02 s run takes at least 1.5 times as long as the 0.04 s run and 2.2 times as long as the 0.08 s run

controls.name: dt-0.02
controls.hypothesis: BioGears' validated step is the reference.
controls.expected: Lactate stays below 2 mM over the first 6 h of the severe infection (in the 48 h run it first exceeds 2 mM at about 16.5 h).

predictions: Pilot (workspace/experiments/timestep-pilot-2026-11-16, every arm): at 6 h, 0.02 / 0.04 / 0.08 s gave lactate 1.53 / 10.28 / 26.1 mM, MAP 99.75 / 99.63 / 99.70 mmHg, blood volume 5877 / 5885 / 5895 mL, blood pathogen 8.744 / 8.742 / 8.736; largest per-sample deviation from 0.02 s: MAP 1.4 / 2.0 mmHg, SBP 1.2 / 2.0, blood volume 11 / 17 mL, pathogen 0.003 / 0.008, tissue integrity 7e-5 / 2e-4; wall time 2459 / 1313 / 866 s (on a 2-core machine with other BioGears runs alongside). The earlier bg-scenario test on the Mac (Fig4_Mild_6h_08) also gave lactate about 26 mM at 0.08 s.
preregistered.thresholds_provenance: Every threshold sits outside the pilot's value with margin; the pilot ran all three arms.
preregistered.pilot: All arms piloted, so these are regression checks.

falsifiability: Refuted if the inflammatory readouts or hemodynamics leave their bands, if lactate does not break at 0.04 and 0.08 s (the 0.02 s run above 2 mM, 0.04 s below 5 mM, or 0.08 s below 0.04 s), or if the larger steps aren't at least 1.5 and 2.2 times faster.
limitations: One infection, one patient, the first 6 h (before the 0.02 s run's own lactate rises); errors may grow over 48 h.
Wall time comes from runs.db (runs_meta completed_at - started_at), so the speed criteria also time the workbench's own overhead; they are ratios, measured on whatever machine runs the study.
